summary:
The engineer's measurement mostly holds up. Their scope matches mine. Their table reproduces byte for byte, and once their section extractor is fixed it gives the same result. The six unfixed defects are really there on NEW, and broader checks I wrote found none of the 'fixed' defects back on NEW, even in other words. I found five problems:
(1) Every regex check can be fooled. I put six defects back into copies of NEW pages in other words, and all six checks still said clean (S49, S50, X6, S25, U43, U44).
(2) The root-quick-start extractor stops at the first '# comment' line inside a code block. For py, rb, perl and elixir it sees only a prefix of the R section. This does not change today's result, because every R check is about the constructor, which comes before the first comment.
(3) D26 is only partly fixed. NEW gates a hand list of 8 rows on optspec. The catalogue's fix (rows from optspec, both ways) is not done: optspec's auth, allow, entity, extend, utility, test and clean have no row.
(4) U44 has per-language lines under the strict reading: 'optional:opMatched list' guard exceptions in ts/test/runtimeforms/py.ts:93 and elixir.ts:97. They are left over from a dropped per-language opMatched fact.
(5) Their claim that the prototype 'never touched' ReadmeRefFeatures.ts or FeatureDocs.ts is false. Commits 81f51194 and eed7d7db changed them (S09 was fixed there). So the six unfixed entries were not out of reach.

Recomputed per entry over 36. With unfixed entries counted on the proposal's side: 2.8% by the brief's rule, 5.6% strict, 16.7% strictest. Counted against the proposal: 22.2%, 25.0% and 36.1%. H3 is not decided, as they said, but the margin against it is wider than they reported.
how_sure: Sure of these: the scope agreement on my 66-entry blind sample, the reproduction, the six fooled checks, the extractor defect, D26's missing rows, and the edits to ReadmeRefFeatures.ts and FeatureDocs.ts. All of them come from commands I ran or files I opened. Moderately sure of the U44 strict move: the lines exist and name the nested-list-match topic, but they are guard exceptions left behind, not lines that carry the fix. Less sure that no other 'once' entry hides a per-language line. I read the 13 Syntax and forms files for facts, notes and exceptions, and used git log -S on entityBy and opMatched, but I did not trace the history of every fact.

These are per-language forms lines that exist because of the nested-list required-match topic. py's Syntax once declared opMatched: { list: 'list(reqmatch, ctrl=None) ...' } (git log -p -S opMatched). Today no provider declares opMatched, the shared sentence carries the fix (sdkdesc.ts:390), and NEW py still shows the optional signature 'list(reqmatch=None, ...)' beside 'The match must include `planet_id`'. So the lines are left over, and the lenient class stays 'once'. That makes 2 languages under strict.

On NEW (B/ts REFERENCE) the constructor table has no row for optspec's auth, allow, entity, extend, utility, test or clean, and utility is the documented transport seam. Their check tests only that a server row exists.

checks_fooled.how: I probed the extracted sections. h3() treats a line starting with '# ' inside a code fence as a heading.
checks_fooled.result: For py, rb, perl and elixir the root quick-start section is cut at the first '# comment' in the code: 1 fence instead of a closed block. Today's verdicts are unaffected, since the constructor comes first. A fence-aware copy (h3check/issuecheck33-fenced.js) gives an identical table. Any future R check about later lines is blind for those four languages.

checks_cannot_fail: None in the 'true on OLD' sense. Every check fires on OLD for at least one language (I reproduced their run, no 'NO OLD SIGNAL' line), and the probe found every needed section and subsection non-empty for all 20 languages, except OLD clojure's constructor table.

Weak in practice: M14's keyIndents only reads blocks where its key regex matches. N04/U06/M04 can only fire for go, since only alias-go2 exists. S13 excludes zig and clojure by hand, on the strength of testMock 'always'.

reading_called_for: H3's refutation test is 'more than about 10% of them still need a per-language edit'. That counts per-language edits, so the unfixed entries belong on the proposal's side of the per-language ratio, because each needs one shared edit. The brief's rule exempts printers every provider declares anyway. On that reading the ratio is 2.8% (5.6% strict), under the line. But H3's claim is 'fixed once, for every language', and a hypothesis is confirmed only when its claim is shown. At the frozen state 7 of 36 entries (19%) are not fixed or only partly fixed. So the right report is: the criterion is not crossed, the claim is not shown, and H3 is not decided. It is not confirmed.
cannot_show: D04 is read only: no variation gives two targets different feature sets.
N04/U06/M04 are shown only for go, through alias-go2. No alias variation exists for the other 12 ported languages.
The seven unported languages (js, php, csharp, java, kotlin, scala, cpp) still use their old components. N11/M35 (js) and every entry's NEW state there can only be measured after their ports.

No compiler is on PATH here for lua, busted, swift, zig, clojure, elixir or ocaml (ported, examples changed), nor for dotnet, kotlinc, scala or sbt (unported). Whether their changed examples compile is not shown. go, python3, ruby, php, perl, javac, rustc, gcc and g++ are present.

Regex checks miss the same defect in other words (6 of 6 attempts fooled). A clean NEW is backed by reading three or more ported pages per entry and by broader code-only and any-wording variants, not by the checks alone.
Only the in-section half of each 'part' entry is measured. M37's README tables, for example, are not.
S13's ts runtime claim ('refuses every request') rests on commit b09502f1; nobody ran it. zig and clojure 'always' rest on their forms citations.
The 'part' entries' out-of-section halves, and the 286 'no' entries, are not measured on NEW.
not_done: I judged blind only the 66 entries ending in 3 or 7. For the other 'no' entries that name README, REFERENCE, quick start or example (146 of them), I only machine-filtered to the 7 whose Where or title names a quick start, REFERENCE, tutorial or quick-start helper, and read those (S05, S30, S46, G07, U75, D25, A01). I did not read all 146.
I did not regenerate any pages. I worked on copies of their out/old and out/new (h3check/out), so the 5 new variations' OLD pages are theirs, unverified.
I did not trace the history of every RefFacts field to check it was not added for one catalogue entry. I did it only for entityBy and opMatched.

I did not check S13's residue: on NEW no-test the test-client text says the client 'refuses every request', then says testopts are 'the test feature's options, which the call switches on' with no test feature present. This may be S13 in other words. I did not score it.

The log REFERENCE section still says 'Set `feature.log.active` to true' although log defaults on (OLD and NEW, all 13 languages I read). I did not score whether this is S09 in other words or a defect the catalogue does not list.
No compiler or example lane was run.
